title: ProviderKind declares exactly thirteen cases in a fixed order that drives every provider list
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Provider.swift:3-16 enum ProviderKind - cases in source order: codex, claude, cursor, opencode, grok, deepseek, meta, zai, devin, antigravity, copilot, commandcode, pi; String-backed, Codable, CaseIterable, Identifiable, Sendable
DroppyCode/Core/Models/Provider.swift:18 var id - id is rawValue
DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift:606 ForEach(ProviderKind.allCases) - the Providers page renders one section per case in allCases order
preconditions: None. The enum is a compile-time constant.
action: Any code enumerates ProviderKind.allCases.
expected_result: Exactly 13 members in this order with these rawValues: codex, claude, cursor, opencode, grok, deepseek, meta, zai, devin, antigravity, copilot, commandcode, pi. Identifiable id equals rawValue.
persistence: The rawValue is the persisted key in providerBinaryPaths, disabledProviders, lastModels, lastEfforts, providerModelCatalogs, providerModelCatalogDates and recentSlashCommands. Renaming a case orphans all of that data.
failure_cases: A rawValue not in this set decodes to nil and the entry is skipped when reading cached catalogs (ProviderRegistry.swift:166).
windows_path: A TypeScript string-literal union with the same 13 literals in the same declaration order, exported as a frozen ordered array for allCases. No platform boundary.
verification_method: unit test asserting the ordered array equals the 13 literals

title: Command Code executable name is cmd, which collides with the Windows command interpreter
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderRegistry.swift:239-247 fallbackExecutables for commandcode - the comment names "cmd" as the documented alias and "command-code" and "commandcode" as the package's own names
action: executable(for:) looks the CLI up on PATH under the bare name cmd, then walks the commandcode fallback list.
expected_result: The bare name searched first is exactly "cmd". The same string is the Binary path placeholder for the Command Code section.
side_effects: A PATH walk plus the fallback candidate walk.
windows_path: PLATFORM BOUNDARY AND COLLISION. On Windows the bare name cmd resolves to the system command interpreter cmd.exe on the machine PATH, so a direct PATHEXT lookup finds the wrong program and would make Command Code read as installed on every Windows PC. The source contains no identity check, so the rule for distinguishing them is an open decision and must not be guessed.
verification_method: contract fixture plus an interaction test proving a system cmd.exe is never accepted as Command Code
